title: Starter Allowance Velocity & SQ Ingestion Automation
creator: Aisha Moreno
description: Design and run an experiment to replace a single fixed starter credit allocation with a velocity-driven microcredit cadence and automate ingestion of enterprise Security Questionnaire (SQ) outcomes to influence onboarding credit behavior. Goal is to improve PD conversion while limiting early churn and reducing cost leakage from abuse.
background: Current starter program grants a one-time fixed credit bundle (e.g., 2,000 tokens) with a 30-day expiry. Early signals show high token burn in first 48 hours with low conversion and several customers requesting negotiated credit addbacks during contract talks (SQ process). We need a flexible credit model that rewards meaningful usage patterns, reduces immediate cost spikes, and surfaces an automated path to bridge PQ/SQ/contract handoffs without manual finance/CS intervention.
goals: Increase 30-day PLG activation-to-paid conversion by +6 percentage points in experiment cohort
Reduce median cost per activated user (first 30 days) by 18% vs baseline
Decrease number of manual CS credit-add requests tied to SQ/contracts by 70%
Maintain NPS for new signups and avoid UX friction from stricter caps
proposed_experiments: Experiment A (Baseline): Existing one-time starter bundle, 30-day expiry (control)

Experiment B (Velocity Microcredits): Seed 500 tokens on signup, then top-ups of 250 tokens when user engages with key activation events (first repo push, first QA call, first model call with structured output). Each top-up expires 14 days from issuance. Top-ups limited to 3 within 30 days.
Experiment C (Sliding Expiry Reset): Same as B but any paid conversion event (billing triggered) resets expiry for remaining credits to 60 days.

Experiment D (SQ-Aware Bridge): For accounts that submit an enterprise SQ and pass minimum security threshold, automatically issue a non-expiring 'contract-bridge' allowance of 1,000 tokens pending contract signature. This allowance is tracked separately and only usable against non-sensitive models (sandbox tier) until legal signoff.
Randomization: 20% Control, 30% B, 30% C, 20% D across free-tier signups from web and API onboarding flows during 6-week experiment window.
instrumentation_requirements: Add events: credit_topup_issued, credit_topup_used, credit_bucket_type, sq_submission, sq_outcome, contract_signed
Experiment labels in analytics: experiment_id, cohort, assignment_timestamp
Cost tracking: per-cohort token cost by model category per day
Fraud signals: rapid multi-account creation, identical payment/contact details, abnormal token burn patterns
rollout_plan: Week 0: Feature flag implementation + backend credit ledger changes (ENG tickets assigned)
Week 1: End-to-end QA, instrumentation smoke tests, and small internal pilot (10 accounts)
Week 2-7: Ramp experiment to target traffic, monitor cost and abuse signals daily
Week 8: Analyze results and recommendations, decide on permanent rollout or iteration
Post-decision: If passed, implement product UI to visualize microcredit cadence in console and update pricing docs
notes: Design trade-off: shorter per-topup expirations directly reduce abuse surface but increase UX messaging complexity.
Legal asked that SQ-based top-ups be segregated in the ledger and marked as contract-bridge to avoid accidental refunds or extended liabilities.
Risk: velocity model could disadvantage low-frequency but high-value eval users; include a monitoring rule to surface large-value low-frequency accounts for manual review.
Budget guardrails: set a daily spend cap for experiment cohorts and automatic rollback threshold at 2.5x expected daily spend.
Feedback from Solutions Engs: prefer a webhook that notifies CS when an account receives an SQ-bridge allowance so they can prioritize outreach.
